body: Workstream succession: dogfood-hardening opened 2026-07-29 as successor to default, which is being marked completed. The default workstream covered project inception through the Task 7 release apparatus and the first published/installed/pinned build g51ff17173bea. Its evidence trail stays reachable via iq-context find; the five substantive captures are cap_20260728T144403Z_c680c66d (second HTV dogfood ingest, full spot-check vs the 1.1 targets plus six findings), cap_20260727T134457Z_16a4f14a (first HTV ingest on the released build), cap_20260727T024600Z_86bdc8f3 (owner dogfood feedback rejecting the receipt-ceremony update model, board convening trigger), cap_20260726T180703Z_6fd7e370 (iq-context relay-back: obligations parser now classifies status by leading token) and cap_20260726T170623Z_e959634b (pin_runtime vs inspect_runtime .claude resolution asymmetry). Nothing was dropped in the carry-over except one duplicated next action, which was merged into the superset spot-check item.

semantic_guidance 1.1 slice — T2 review findings (2026-07-29). Codex review returned clean on all six focus areas. Independent Claude review returned 1 blocking + 8 advisory. BLOCKING (accepted, fixed): rule 4's 'wherever such a proposal's substance appears in any field' with an illustrative em-dash list licenses recording a rejected proposal as an action_item with an inline disposition — passes S6 but fails S5, which is none_match on $.action_items[*].action with no disposition exemption. S5 passes today, so this would have converted a green blocking assertion red, discoverable only after a receipt and a fresh acceptance run. Fixed by making the action prohibition explicitly uncurable ('stating its disposition inline does not make it eligible') and scoping sentence 2 to 'any other field'. KEY STRUCTURAL INSIGHT (accepted, drove two fixes): the extraction agent obeys semantic_guidance_rules carried in the request; docs/artifact-contract.md is NOT shipped in the request. Precision that lives only in the contract does no work at extraction time. Consequences: rule 4 must name the disposition vocabulary inline because S6's regex set is closed (shelved/on hold/tabled/not moving forward all fail it), and rule 5 must enumerate the identity-bearing fields (stakeholder name, summary, quoted evidence text) rather than use the undefined term — evidence.text is the non-obvious one, since a signal with a fully-resolved stakeholder_name but an ambiguous alias in its evidence quote must still score low. ALSO ACCEPTED: S6's guidance_rule pointer moves 3 to 4 (under 1.1 the inline-disposition clause it tests is rule 4; S7/S8 correctly stay at 3); product-status.md:49/52, README.md:31 and implementation-plan.md:126 overclaim by asserting 1.1 as shipped capability and pairing it with 1.0-era dev-run evidence, all qualified; rule 6 gets a binding framing-restraint clause in artifact-contract.md so no shipped rule lacks contract basis; two new guard tests added because the contract now states published-version immutability while enforcement was only a code comment, and five-surface parity is manual with much more prose to keep byte-identical. DECLINED: rule 5 forcing low confidence on a signal whose evidence quote merely contains the alias is inherent to S10's assertion design, not a 1.1 defect; the 2026-07-26 dev-run session log citing the fixture at 1.0 stays unamended because session logs are frozen records and git preserves the state. VERIFIED CLEAN by both reviewers: 1.0 tuple byte-identical to HEAD, 35/35 verbatim rule hits across the five surfaces, expected-review.json structurally diffed with exactly three changes and no selector/pattern/operator/severity weakened, the rewritten older-published-version test proven non-circular and stronger than what it replaced.

Release-evidence acceptance attempt 2 (2026-07-29T21:13-21:17Z, build meeting-ingest-0.2.0-g3695fc350c77-s61e1660c5dc8): 18/18 blocking, 1/1 advisory, release evidence, no interventions, no development override. THE ATTEMPT 1 PRECONDITION IS ESTABLISHED: host cache verified BEFORE the run by a provenance-only probe of the session-provider agent in a separate context (no extraction, no file access) that reported exactly one rule set, version 1.1, 7 rules, rule 6 present, rules 4/5 revised; quoted rule 4/5/6 text then matched ~/.claude installed doc verbatim. Agent sha 890878d7 identical across repo source, user-level install, and acceptance-root copy; workflow.match true, 8/8 pin and 8/8 receipt comparisons. readiness ready with ZERO findings. Grounding matched fixture exactly (3 labels, 36 timestamps). meeting_id mtg-20260726-6c45c41d, same as attempt 1, so artifacts are comparable. 14 signals vs attempt 1's 11. EVALUATOR REBUILT: the prior evaluator lived in a dead session scratchpad, so it was rewritten from the declared evaluation block and verified twice before its tally was trusted -- synthetic self-test detecting violations for all 8 executable operators in both directions, plus 7/7 targeted mutations of THIS run's own snapshot (DG1,S1,S3,S5,S6,S10,S12) each flipping its named assertion off a clean baseline. ATTEMPT 1 DEFECTS FIXED: the Femi/Dara misattribution is gone (T2 credits Dara, evidence row agrees), and the Thursday-scope overreach is gone (A3 reads 'same deadline as the log pull', matching Femi at 03:37). BUT RULE 6 WAS VIOLATED: blind review (cross-vendor codex, read-only, isolated dir, fixture filename preserved, never saw expected-review.json) found A2/D3/T5/TL;DR/one signal render Rosa's committed scope as 'raise the merge timeout AND add an alert' when Rosa narrowed it at 02:16 ('That I will take. Alerting change only, no loader logic') and self-summarized at 03:42 ('alerting change is mine by Friday') -- she labels her own commitment 'alerting change' twice and never restates the timeout raise. Upheld as rule 6 scope widening inside a committed action item; ownership and Friday date are correct, only scope is widened. This is the FIRST evidence rule 6 is not reliably obeyed on the approved runtime, caught only by blind review, which is the already-recorded blind spot. Two lesser blind findings: Q5 assigns Rosa a group conditional (same pattern as attempt 1 finding 4, softened not eliminated), ASK5 records Femi's group proposal as an ask directed to Rosa. TWO DEFECTS BEYOND THE ASSERTIONS: (1) artifact front matter self-contradicts -- generated_by reads 'meeting-ingest 0.1.0' while runtime_provenance.semantic_version reads 0.2.0, because render.py:35 declares tool_version dataclass default '0.1.0' that NO caller anywhere sets, and tests/fixtures/expected_markdown/summary_plus_verbatim_basic.md:20 pins the same 0.1.0 so the suite enforces the bug -- a THIRD version source after BUILD_INFO, present at HEAD, affecting every artifact the released build renders; (2) ~/.codex/skills/meeting-ingest/SKILL.md still carries guidance 1.0 (6 rules, pre-revision 4/5, no framing rule) vs repo source 1.1 -- the non-receipt-managed Codex pair was never re-installed after the 1.1 propagation, so the procedure's byte-identical check FAILS; did not affect this run since Claude Code is the host. Third finding: the evaluator is rebuilt ad hoc every run and belongs in the repo. HUMAN SEMANTIC REVIEW OUTSTANDING -- not milestone proof until the owner completes it. Acceptance root RETAINED at /var/folders/x8/kppzllb928x2qd_7hqvs2k1c0000gn/T/meeting-ingest-acceptance.3ffNBK pending that review. Record: docs/sessions/2026-07-29-guidance-1_1-release-evidence-acceptance.md

RELAY ANSWER (second inbound of the same ~/.claude relay; the first was answered earlier on 2026-07-29 and this session produced stronger evidence for the same conclusion). The relay asserts semantic_guidance 1.1 was HAND-APPLIED to the receipt-managed installed agent doc and asks a fork: is 1.1 published on our side. ANSWER TO THE FORK: YES. Published as build meeting-ingest-0.2.0-g3695fc350c77-s61e1660c5dc8, receipt sha256 312ce10c5c6ca61a516b9335511f249537dae1b44968782f5797d6a0824e0e52, private-alpha channel advanced 2026-07-29T19:06:27Z. BUT THE RELAY'S PREMISE IS FALSE and its recommended remedy is therefore unnecessary. The installed copy did NOT arrive as a hand-edit; it arrived via scripts/install-approved-skill.py driven by that receipt at 15:07 local. Evidence gathered independently during the release-evidence acceptance run today: (1) ~/.claude/agents/meeting-ingest-session-provider.md sha256 890878d76b21e29b65d8e6e4ce6044aa36ca4e3373a83149f388aacd1b565584, byte-identical to the repo source docs/claude-agents/meeting-ingest-session-provider.md and to a fresh receipt-verified install into a temporary acceptance root; (2) meeting-ingest runtime inspect reports workflow.match true with ALL 8 pin comparisons and ALL 8 receipt comparisons matching; (3) readiness --host claude-code returns ready with ZERO findings and no workflow_hash_mismatch, which is the exact failure a hand-edit would produce by design. The relay's own note that both files were already dirty when its session opened is consistent with the 15:07 installer write. So this is 'same bytes by provenance', not 'same bytes by coincidence'. CORRECT ACTION IN ~/.claude: commit those two files. That repo's HEAD simply predates the install; the working tree is the receipt-verified content. Do NOT revert (that would destroy correct installed content and trip workflow_hash_mismatch) and do NOT reinstall (provenance is already receipt-derived and verifiable). The rendered skill 7e2c1ae47dc642ebc871f68f699c823a431fdf8d53e879c3a12a8927e4de6dc3 is the installer's rendered output with the executable marker substituted, identical at both destinations, so a byte comparison against the repo template is meaningless for that file by design. THE GAP THE RELAY RAISES IS LEGITIMATE and already an open question in this workstream: an installed copy carries no receipt/build/content stamp of its own, so a hand-edit is undetectable from the consumer side by inspecting the file alone -- though NOT undetectable from the tooling side, since readiness and runtime inspect both catch it against the pin and receipt. That is the real answer to 'is it worth a stamp': the detection already exists, it just lives in the CLI rather than in the document. The SKILL.md five-surface duplication question the relay raises is likewise already an open question. Model pin untouched, model: claude-opus-5, Decision 33 intact -- confirmed.

Committed the two receipt-installed workflow artifacts in ~/.claude as d37c9e1 (chore(meeting-ingest): track receipt-installed guidance 1.1 artifacts), closing the relay thread. Decisive fact found on inspection: ~/.claude/.gitignore lines 22-25 explicitly un-ignore agents/ and skills/ (!agents/**, !skills/**), so that repo has already decided it tracks these files. That rules out the alternative of untracking them as installer-owned build output, and makes committing the correct action rather than merely the tidy one. Scoped strictly to the two meeting-ingest files: ~/.claude also had NINE unrelated dirty files (six commands/iq-*.md, settings.json, .iq-context/focus-state.json, .iq-context/workstreams/agent-orchestration/captures.jsonl) from the iq-context v0.5.1 command surface work, and a broad git add -A would have swept them in. Verified before committing that the diff is confined to the semantic guidance rules block (1.0 to 1.1, rule 4 widened to parked proposals, rule 5 extended, new rule 6, old 6 renumbered to 7) and that the model pin is untouched at claude-opus-5, so Decision 33 is intact. Verified after committing that the install chain is unaffected: runtime inspect from HTV reports workflow.match true with agent sha 890878d7 and skill sha 7e2c1ae4 unchanged, 8/8 pin and 8/8 receipt comparisons matching, and readiness returns ready_with_history_warnings with no workflow_hash_mismatch, the standing legacy-corpus history findings being the only ones. RECURRENCE, now recorded as a next action: because ~/.claude tracks installer output, every release will dirty these paths again and leave the same false hand-edit signal that misled the relay twice. The fix is to fold 'commit the ~/.claude installed artifacts' into the release flow rather than leaving it to be rediscovered after the fact.

RELAY ISSUE #1 IMPLEMENTED, commit ea9b157 (docs(relay): stand up the relay intake lane). All four deliverables shipped: (1) triage poll wired into BOTH AGENTS.md Start Here and CLAUDE.md — CLAUDE.md matters because Claude Code auto-loads only CLAUDE.md, so a poll living solely in AGENTS.md would never fire in Claude sessions (claude-implementer review finding, accepted); the step reads each open relay with gh issue view since the list shows titles only; (2) relay label pre-existing; (3) .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/relay.md adapted from iq-context cf60578 with this project's kinds (dogfood finding, pipeline bug, extraction-quality report, feature ask); (4) README line at the end of Relationship To iQ Context. DESIGN QUESTION ANSWERED YES: the template's new Target section distinguishes defects against a shipped build from requests against the source repo; a shipped-build defect must cite build.build_id and receipt.sha256 from 'meeting-ingest runtime inspect --json' — verified against source as the ONE command printing both (runtime.py:832-837); plain runtime inspect omits the receipt sha (cli.py:351-356) and readiness --json carries no receipt key at all, its runtime_provenance_sha256 being a different digest a filer would silently mistake for it (readiness.py:242). That wrong-command guidance was the T2 blocking finding, caught independently by BOTH reviewers (codex P2 + claude-implementer blocking) and fixed before commit. NOT DONE, owner-gated: push (joins the 7 pending commits as 8th) and closing issue #1 — the template only takes effect on GitHub once pushed, so close after push. The first-content-issue refile (catalog-as-native-tooling) is the REQUESTING project's move: the draft lives in iq-context's context, so an iq-context session refiles it once the lane is live on GitHub. Issue: https://github.com/BIWizzard/meeting-ingest/issues/1

Global skill file-dogfood-relay installed at ~/.claude/skills/file-dogfood-relay (commit b9f0515 in ~/.claude), validated by skill-creator packaging. Any meeting-ingest consumer project can now say 'file the dogfood relay' or 'send dogfood' and the agent files a relay issue on BIWizzard/meeting-ingest per .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/relay.md: provenance from runtime inspect --json ONLY (build.build_id + receipt.sha256, guarding the readiness --json lookalike-digest trap that was the T2 blocking finding on issue #1), full run report in Concrete driver with minimum-evidence quoting (third-party sensitivity guard), gh issue create --label relay, then local capture of the issue URL. Owner is using the equivalent one-off prompt for the immediate HTV report; the skill is the durable path.

SPOT-CHECK of relay issue #2 artifact (mtg-20260803-9171ca70, guidance 1.1, shipped 0.2.0 build): owner-side line-by-line read of artifact + 11 signals against the verbatim transcript CONFIRMS the filer's 'no extraction issues' claim. (B) Enum/vocabulary drift on the same build: meeting_type 'working session' (#2) vs 'working_session' (#3); signal/table status values are free text ('declined by Ken', 'rejected alternative') — the status-vocabulary gap extends beyond the Decisions table into the signal JSONL schema; evidence-locator zero-padding also drifts (0:52 vs 00:03). WISPR FLOW A/B DOGFOOD (owner-run blind test, HTV consumer, 2026-08-04): same ~58-min Migration Sync meeting ingested twice on the 0.2.0 build — Teams VTT (mtg-20260804-2fa72325, 131KB source) vs Wispr Flow markdown-export saved as .txt (mtg-20260804-3d2dfcd0, 53KB). Both runs completed end-to-end, date gate exercised via manual override both times. HEADLINE DEFECT: the Wispr run produced ZERO signals (0-line JSONL, artifact renders 'None identified') while the VTT run produced 12 from the same conversation — and the Wispr artifact's own tables hold 8 commitments, 6 asks, 9 risks, so candidates were extracted but never became signals; an empty signal stream on a content-rich meeting passed validation silently. Guard candidate: consistency check flagging zero signals when decisions/commitments are non-empty. Root cause unconfirmable because BOTH runs' provider request/response cache pairs were deleted (cache dirs cleared ~13:51, while a stray 2026-07-07 response survives) — inconsistent cache retention also means the evidence paths cited in relay issue #3 no longer exist. SECOND FINDING: extraction recall variance favoring the cleaner source — Wispr artifact has 14 topics/7 decisions vs VTT 10/3, and at least three VTT-run misses (Fast CP ~100M-row 4-second copy method, the 'present the most cumbersome version to the team' decision at 37:03, the WideOrbit-pipeline-writes-to-UAT risk at 57:27) are PROVABLY present in the VTT transcript text, so this is extraction variance under a noisier transcript, not transcript fidelity. THIRD FINDING: identity split — same humans got different person IDs across the two runs (person-ken-graham from Teams roster labels vs person-kenneth-graham from Wispr voice names); no cross-source identity normalization exists, so the corpus now holds one person under two IDs; also the Wispr attendee table renders Raw Speaker Labels as 'Unknown' although the transcript carries explicit name labels — a small attendee-table defect. POSITIVE: the Wispr diarization phantom (Speaker 4, two interjections the VTT attributes to Baba) was handled exactly per the guidance 1.1 identity-confidence rule — surfaced honestly as 'Unidentified fourth speaker', low confidence — this is the real-world identity-ambiguity evidence the standing next action was waiting for; that item can be retired. TRANSCRIPT QUALITY: Wispr materially better text (correct names in speech where Teams garbled — 'Kushali does her own' vs VTT 'Charlie does our own', 'Baba tells them' vs 'Boyd tells them'; real punctuation, per-utterance timestamps, fillers preserved) but weaker speaker identity than Teams roster labels. EFFICIENCY: VTT source is 2.5x the bytes for identical content (caption-cue overhead + utterance fragmentation), consistent with the owner's much-higher token burn on the VTT run; output side reverses (Wispr artifact 716 lines vs 453) due to finer segmentation. Vocab drift note: meeting_type 'working session' (space) on both today's runs vs 'working_session' in mtg-20260803-a9d3c1a3 — the drift is run-level nondeterminism, not source-format-dependent. CORPUS NOTE for the consumer: the same real meeting now exists twice with different meeting_ids and asymmetric signal streams; any dedup is the consumer's move and OB-002-1 gates corpus mutation on an adoption plan.

T1 codex review returned 5 findings (P1: person-ID path traversal into corpus; P2s: word-splitting on IDs, date-source disagreement with catalog on one 07-10/07-13 file, unencoded spaces in link destinations, tab corruption of TSV); fix round dispatched to the implementer with the ruling that views match the catalog's filename-date rule. IDENTITY DRIFT QUANTIFIED, much worse than the A/B showed: Ken under FOUR IDs (person-ken-graham 48, ken-graham, person-kenneth-graham, graham-ken-contractor), Baba under three (person-opeyemi-baba 26, person-baba-opeyemi 16, opeyemi-baba), Jean Francois under three including a hardan/harden misspelling pair; four artifacts carry unprefixed IDs; 13 attendee rows are null/Unresolved extractor failures (12 in the 2026-07-20 standup — spot-check target); 111 of 166 artifacts predate attendee tables. This hard-quantifies the cross-source identity normalization next action and adds the interim consumer-side fix: an alias map consumed by gen-views. Series enum drift also quantified: daily_standup/daily standup/daily stand-up/recurring daily stand-up render as separate series — feeds the status/enum vocabulary next action.

GEN-VIEWS FIX ROUND LANDED: all 5 codex findings verified against the code and fixed by the implementer, none rejected. P1 path traversal was REAL AND EXPLOITABLE — probe confirmed an attendee ID of ../../pwned escaped _derived and would have overwritten a corpus artifact; fixed by constraining IDs to ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ with dropped-ID reporting (all 61 real IDs already conform). Hostile-fixture proof: traversal victim file SHA-identical, spaced filenames render with angle-bracket destinations, tabs stripped with no column shift. Views now use the catalog's filename-date rule (07-10 file consistent; comm -3 shows zero date disagreements across all 166 rows); implementer correctly left the front-matter-date fallback out as unreachable under the catalog-inherited exclusion rule. Re-verification: byte-identical reruns, 642 links zero broken, 166/166/166 count reconciliation, corpus untouched. DOGFOOD LESSON FOR THE ENGINE ROADMAP: attendee-table fields are LLM-extracted text — any consumer tooling (and any future native views/catalog feature) must treat artifact-derived identifiers as untrusted input for path construction; worth a line in the eventual views/catalog design. Alias map remains the queued next piece, pending owner go-ahead.

OWNER RULING (2026-08-06, verbatim intent): shipped means running. If we build, deploy, and publish core functionality, consumers HAVE it — no silent consumer-side opt-in for features on the features-and-benefits list. Trigger: discovery that Layer 5A identity registry + derivation-time resolution shipped implemented in the 0.2.0 build but never activated at the reference consumer — no init scaffolding of _playbook-state/, no workflow step invoking playbook derivation, readiness filing the absence as optional_playbook_output_missing (a severity that trains everyone to ignore it; the orchestrator itself stepped past it all week). Owner assumed the identity feature was live because product-truth surfaces say 'implemented' with no activation state. This is the clearest Just Works Continuity (record 002) violation to date and it is a DELIVERY-MODEL defect, not an identity-feature defect: the identity design itself (human-owned registry, no fuzzy auto-merge, candidate review) is sound and stays — auto-ACTIVATION with human-in-the-loop REVIEW are compatible. Fix shape to ratify: (1) release evidence must include ACTIVATION evidence at the reference consumer, not just install/chain verification — a release is not complete until the feature's behavior is observable; (2) init and update scaffold required state; post-ingest triggers or loudly nags derivation; (3) readiness gets a core-inactive category distinct from optional/history; (4) product-status distinguishes implemented vs delivered/active per consumer class. Belongs in the queued update-policy board brief amending record 002 (same consumer-class segmentation conversation). MEANWHILE, consumer-side state as of now: registry seeded at HTV (_playbook-state/stakeholders.toml, 15 entries all status=proposed, 61 IDs to 33 people, verification clean, registry-SHA untouched by generation runs — human-owned honored); owner review of proposed entries deliberately deferred — owner rejected the review prompt mid-anger, do not re-ask; views resolve through the registry; refresh-views.sh is the one post-ingest command; first playbook derivation run still pending.
